5	# Data saving and commits
6	
7	Editors update application state immediately. `CommitBatcher` later coalesces repeatable edits into durable repository writes.
8	
9	## Batched save flow
10	
11	```text
12	Editor change
13	  → domain service updates in-memory state
14	  → CommitBatcher replaces that domain object's pending change
15	  → configured delay or explicit flush
16	  → renderer registers exact expected present/absent persistence outcomes
17	  → StorageService.commit creates one repository commit
18	  → optional automatic push
19	  → committed files and path changes are reconciled into application state
20	```
21	
22	`DataService.init` creates one batcher per project. Every scheduled change restarts one global trailing `react.autoCommitDelayMs` timer (30 seconds by default). This timer policy is unchanged by action identity handling.
23	
24	Pending cards use `Card.header.internalId`; pending actions use `ActionDefinition.id`; generic files use their path. Keys include change kind, preventing card, action, and file identities from colliding. Card and action paths are mutable persistence metadata.
25	
26	When flushing starts, `CommitBatcher` synchronously transfers the complete pending collection into an isolated active batch and installs a new empty pending collection. Edits received during persistence enter only the new collection. Active success discards the active batch without object-reference comparison. A successful path change rebases only newer pending source-path metadata for the same identity. Active failure restores entries only when no newer entry for that identity exists.
27	
28	A single `CommitRequest` passes both ordinary writes (`files`) and path replacements (`moves`: old path, new path, and latest content) to `StorageService.commit`.
29	
30	## Editor behavior
31	
32	### Cards and Markdown
33	
34	Card body, title, header, ordering, and policy edits update loaded files, then `CardOperations.saveFile` schedules them. All files share the batcher: editing two cards before a flush produces one request with both latest versions and a combined message.
35	
36	### Actions and filenames
37	
38	`ActionService` owns drafts by action ID, including current source path and desired target path. It also owns field and graph validation, serialization, and renderer publication. Each persistable change passes its action ID through `DataService.persistActionFile`; later committed edits replace pending content for that same ID. Non-persistable drafts stay in memory until repaired or discarded.
39	
40	An action's filename follows its label:
41	
42	1. Trim and lowercase the label.
43	2. Replace each run of non-ASCII-lowercase-letter-or-digit characters with `-`.
44	3. Remove leading and trailing `-` characters.
45	4. Add `.json` under the configured actions folder.
46	5. If another action owns the path, append `-2`, `-3`, and so on.
47	
48	For example, `Review Feature!` becomes `actions/review-feature.json`.
49	
50	Filename and content changes share the batch:
51	
52	| Situation | Result |
53	| --- | --- |
54	| Persisted source | One path replacement containing the latest JSON. |
55	| New action not yet stored | One path change targets the final filename; storage writes the target even when the source is absent. |
56	| Repeated label edits before flush | Only the final target path and content remain. |
57	| Typing during an active rename | The next pending change is rebased from the committed target path. |
58	
59	Renaming keeps the action's stable `id`, so chains, schedules, execution requests, histories, and conversation logs do not change. After storage confirms the move, `ActionService` re-keys path-indexed file, definition, and publication metadata. Draft and open-document ownership remains on action ID, preserving tab position, active state, and Markdown undo history.
60	
61	## Flushing and state
62	
63	`DataService.flushPendingChanges` adds valid action drafts, then flushes the batch. Deleted or invalid drafts block it until repaired, re

mediate operations
86	
87	Commands needing an immediate repository result bypass `CommitBatcher`: creating cards or folders, deleting files, moving release files, saving project or schedule configuration, and adding or removing Git worktrees.
88	
89	Callers flush first when ordering matters. Typing-driven updates must use the batcher.
90	
91	All writes into the primary worktree, renderer saves and desktop writes (activity, schedules, usage metrics, token usage) alike, share `ProjectOperationCoordinator`, which serializes project-wide operations by repository root. Renderer saves take it outside the Git index lock. Desktop writes that do not commit are tracked in `UncommittedProjectWrites`; worktree integration commits them once inside the lock, then rebases, squashes, cleans up the branch and writes the integration history before releasing it, so no primary-worktree file changes during integration.
92	
93	## Storage backends
94	
95	All renderer workflows use `StorageService`:
96	
97	| Backend | Commit behavior |
98	| --- | --- |
99	| Local Electron | Sends `CommitRequest` through the preload bridge. `desktop/src/project/project_files.js` moves an existing source or writes the target directly when source is absent. A tracked, already-absent source deletion is staged before one Git commit. |
100	| GitHub | Creates content blobs, then one tree containing additions, updates, move targets, and null entries only for move sources present in the current tree. It creates one pending commit from that tree. |
101	| Remote control | Forwards the same request to the connected desktop host, which applies local missing-source behavior. |
102	
103	Renderer persistence tracking registers outcomes before watcher-producing storage calls. Writes expect exact target content; moves expect an absent
104	source and exact target content; file and known folder descendants expect absence after deletion. Latest outcome owns each normalized repository path.
105	Operation settlement does not consume outcomes and does not wait for watcher delivery.
106	
107	Watcher callbacks defer a tracked path while any local operation affecting it remains unresolved, then inspect current persisted state. Exact matches
108	are local echoes: repository-path bookkeeping may update, but action and Markdown domain state do not reload. Contradictions use existing external
109	reload and conflict handling. Project/branch replacement discards old-scope outcomes; watcher restoration verifies retained outcomes during full
110	resynchronization. Local Electron and remote-control storage share this renderer behavior. GitHub storage has no watcher and bypasses tracking.
111	
112	## Main implementation files
113	
114	| File | Responsibility |
115	| --- | --- |
116	| `app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts` | Coalescing, delay, serialized flushes, retries, and path-change rebasing. |
117	| `app/src/services/data/data_service.ts` | Batch lifecycle, action persistence gateway, save state, and flushing. |
118	| `app/src/services/data/card_operations.ts` | File scheduling, storage commits, direct state reconciliation, and automatic push. |
119	| `app/src/services/project/expected_persistence_outcomes.ts` | Project-scoped expected outcomes, unresolved operations, matching, bounds, and reset. |
120	| `app/src/services/project/expected_persistence_storage.ts` | Central outcome derivation around watcher-producing storage mutations. |
121	| `app/src/services/project/project_loading.ts` | Watcher classification, external reload routing, and restoration verification. |
122	| `app/src/services/actions/action_service.ts` | Action drafts, validation, filename selection, and post-commit path reconciliation. |
123	| `app/src/services/project/save_state_service.ts` | Queued and active save tracking. |
124	| `app/src/data/data_types.ts` | `CommitRequest`, file, move, and storage contracts. |
125	| `app/src/services/github/github_storage_writer.ts` | GitHub blob, tree, and commit persistence. |
126	| `desktop/src/project/project_files.js` | Local writes, Git moves, staging, and commits. |

2	import { getElectronActionBridge } from '../../data/electron_action_bridge'
3	import type { AgentConversation } from '../../data/data_types'
4	import { actionRunRegistry } from '../actions/action_run_registry'
5	import { dialogService } from '../dialog_service'
6	import { register } from '../service_injector'
7	
8	const UNSEEN_STATUSES = new Set<ActionRunStatus>(['completed', 'failed', 'waitingForInput'])
9	const PROJECT_SCOPE_KEY = 'project'
10	
11	type ResolveStoredConversation = (conversation: AgentConversation) => AgentConversation | null
12	export type AgentConversationScope = string | null
13	
14	/** Event type dispatched for aggregate acknowledgement changes on one card. */
15	export function cardAcknowledgementEvent(cardInternalId: string) {
16	    return `card-${cardInternalId}`
17	}
18	
19	/** Event type dispatched for acknowledgement changes on one card action. */
20	export function actionAcknowledgementEvent(cardInternalId: string, actionId: string) {
21	    return `action-${cardInternalId}-${actionId}`
22	}
23	
24	/** Event type dispatched for project-origin conversation changes. */
25	export const PROJECT_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_EVENT = 'project-conversations'
26	
27	function conversationKey(scope: AgentConversationScope, actionId: string, conversationId: string) {
28	    return `${scope ?? PROJECT_SCOPE_KEY}-${actionId}-${conversationId}`
29	}
30	
31	/** Resolves the backend write before any local value changes, so a missing backend leaves the record untouched. */
32	function requireConversationViewedWriter() {
33	    const bridge = getElectronActionBridge()
34	    if (!bridge?.updateActionConversationViewed) throw new Error('Updating conversation view state requires Electron')
35	
36	    return (reference: string, viewed: boolean) => bridge.updateActionConversationViewed!(reference, viewed)
37	}
38	
39	/**
40	 * Tracks chat visibility and persists conversation view state.
41	 * Changes are announced through scoped card and card-action events so only affected leaves update;
42	 * the conversation data itself lives in the agent integration store and the activity files.
43	 * Scoping uses the stable card internal ID so card renames cannot break acknowledgement state.
44	 */
45	export class AgentAcknowledgementService extends EventTarget {
46	    private readonly backendViewedByConversationId = new Map<string, boolean>()
47	    private readonly lastRunStatuses = new Map<string, ActionRunStatus>()
48	    private resolveStoredConversation: ResolveStoredConversation | null = null
49	    private readonly visibleEntries = new Map<string, Set<string>>()
50	
51	    constructor() {
52	        super()
53	        actionRunRegistry.subscribeActiveRunEvents(this.handleActionRunEvent)
54	    }
55	
56	    /** Connects the loaded-conversation store so view changes land on the canonical conversation records. */
57	    connectConversationStore(resolveStoredConversation: ResolveStoredConversation) {
58	        this.resolveStoredConversation = resolveStoredConversation
59	    }
60	
61	    /** Announce acknowledgement-relevant conversation changes to the scoped card and card-action subscribers. */
62	    announceConversationsChanged(scope: AgentConversationScope, actionIds: string[]) {
63	        if (scope === null) {
64	            this.dispatchEvent(new Event(PROJECT_ACKNOWLEDGEMENT_EVENT))
65	            return
66	        }
67	
68	        for (const actionId of new Set(actionIds)) {
69	            this.dispatchEvent(new Event(actionAcknowledgementEvent(scope, actionId)))
70	        }
71	        this.dispatchEvent(new Event(cardAcknowledgementEvent(scope)))
72	    }
73	
74	    setConversationVisible(
75	        entryId: string,
76	        scope: AgentConversationScope,
77	        actionId: string,
78	        conversation: AgentConversation,
79	        visible: boolean,
80	    ) {
81	        const key = conversationKey(scope, actionId, conversation.id)
82	        const entries = this.visibleEntries.get(key) ?? new Set<string>()
83	        if (visible) entries.add(entryId)
84	        else entries.delete(entryId)
85	        if (entries.size > 0) this.visibleEntries.set(key, entries)
86	        else this.visibleEntries.delete(key)

88	        if (visible && !current.viewed) {
89	            void this.setViewed(scope, actionId, conversation, true).catch(() => undefined)
90	        }
91	    }
92	
93	    /**
94	     * Remembers the view state the backend last reported for a conversation, so a failed write has a
95	     * value to fall back to rather than guessing from the optimistic one it is undoing.
96	     */
97	    recordBackendViewed(conversationId: string, viewed: boolean) {
98	        this.backendViewedByConversationId.set(conversationId, viewed)
99	    }
100	
101	    /**
102	     * Applies the view state locally first so the window it was clicked in responds without waiting for
103	     * the backend, then persists it. A failed write puts back the value the backend last reported, which
104	     * leaves no window showing a state the activity file does not hold. The backend announcement that
105	     * follows a successful write replaces the optimistic value, so a differing backend value wins.
106	     */
107	    async setViewed(scope: AgentConversationScope, actionId: string, conversation: AgentConversation, viewed: boolean) {
108	        const current = this.resolveStoredConversation?.(conversation) ?? conversation
109	        if (current.viewed === viewed) return current
110	
111	        const previous = current.viewed
112	        let applied = false
113	        try {

115	            current.viewed = viewed
116	            conversation.viewed = viewed

120	        } catch (error) {
121	            if (applied) {

123	                current.viewed = reverted
124	                conversation.viewed = reverted
125	                this.announceConversationsChanged(scope, [actionId])

130	            dialogService.error(error, { fallbackMessage })
131	            throw error
132	        }
133	
134	        return current
135	    }
136	
137	    /** Clears transient state at a project boundary. */
138	    reset() {
139	        this.backendViewedByConversationId.clear()
140	        this.lastRunStatuses.clear()
141	        this.visibleEntries.clear()
142	    }
143	
144	    private readonly handleActionRunEvent = (event: ActionRunEvent) => {
145	        const previousStatus = this.lastRunStatuses.get(event.runId)
146	        this.lastRunStatuses.set(event.runId, event.status)
147	        if (previousStatus === event.status || !UNSEEN_STATUSES.has(event.status)) return
148	
149	        const conversation = actionRunRegistry.getRunStore(event.runId)?.getSnapshot().conversation ?? null
150	        const scope = event.context.cardInternalId ?? null
151	        const actionId = conversation?.actionId
152	        if (!conversation || !actionId) return
153	        if ((this.visibleEntries.get(conversationKey(scope, actionId, conversation.id))?.size ?? 0) > 0) return
154	
155	        void this.setViewed(scope, actionId, conversation, false).catch(() => undefined)
156	    }

Analysis done. Plan below. No edits yet.

## Change Plan (F_429)

**Root cause (confirmed):** `setViewed` writes the activity file on the desktop side after the run's own commit. That write is only recorded in `UncommittedProjectWrites`, so it stays uncommitted until the next integration.

**Block 1: Commit-only path in the renderer batch**
- `app/src/data/data_types.ts`: add `paths?: string[]` to `CommitRequest`.
- `app/src/data/commit_batcher.ts`:
  - Add a new change kind `CommitPathChange { kind: 'path'; path }` with key `path:${path}`. Two schedules for the same path collapse into one pending entry.
  - `commitActiveBatch`: `path` changes skip `serializeChange` and go into `request.paths`. `paths` is added to the request only when it is non-empty.
  - The after-commit loop (acknowledge, `onPersisted`, `onPathCommitted`) handles only serialized changes.
  - `hasPendingFile` and `discardPendingFile` already match a `path` change, because `changeSourcePath` and `changeTargetPath` fall through to `change.path`. No change needed there.
- `app/src/services/data/data_service.ts`: add `scheduleRepositoryPathCommit(path, message)`, shaped like `scheduleFileCommit`.
- `expected_persistence_storage.ts` and `card_operation_context.ts`: no edit needed. Both iterate only `files` and `moves`, so `paths` already produces no outcomes and no `recordCurrentContent` call.

**Block 2: Schedule after a successful view write**
- `agent_acknowledgement_service.ts` `setViewed`: after the `try` block succeeds, get the activity path with `parseConversationActivityReference(conversation.path)` and call `scheduleRepositoryPathCommit(activityPath, 'Update conversation view state')`.
- I'll get `dataService` through `getService<DataService>('dataService')` with a type-only import. `action_run_registry.ts` already does this. A direct import would create an import cycle, because `data_service.ts` imports `agentAcknowledgementService`.
- If the write fails, the `catch` block rethrows, so nothing is scheduled.
- **Spec gap:** the spec doesn't say what to do if scheduling itself throws after a successful write (for example, no project open). My proposal: put the scheduling outside the write's `try` block and report the error via `dialogService.error`. Then a scheduling error does not undo the view state that was already saved. Confirm or redirect.

**Block 3: Desktop staging**
- `desktop/src/project/project_files.js` `commitNow`: for each entry in `request.paths`:
  - throw on a non-string or empty value;
  - resolve it with `ensureInsideRoot`;
  - skip it when `pathExists` is false;
  - otherwise run `git add -- <path>`.
- This runs before the existing `commitStagedChanges`, which commits once and does nothing when nothing changed.

**Block 4: GitHub rejection**
- `github_storage_writer.ts` `commit`: throw `'Commit-only paths require the local Git bridge'` when `request.paths` is non-empty.

**Block 5: Architecture doc**
- `design/architecture/data_saving_and_commits.md`: add a short section on commit-only paths: what they are, the snapshot-overwrite reason, and that GitHub rejects them.

**Block 6: Tests**
- `commit_batcher.test.ts`:
  - a `path` change lands in `request.paths`, not in `files`;
  - two schedules for one path give one entry;
  - a failed flush puts the entry back.
- `agent_acknowledgement_service.node.test.ts`: register a fake `dataService`, then check:
  - a successful write schedules the activity path for both `true` and `false`;
  - a failed write schedules nothing.
- `project_files.test.mjs`: use a real temp Git repo, because the spec asks for the on-disk content to be committed. Check:
  - a commit-only path is committed with its disk content;
  - a missing path is skipped and the commit still succeeds.
  - This test runs real `git`, which AGENTS.md lists as a temporary-test trigger. The spec explicitly requires the test, though. Alternative: mock `GitProcess` like the existing move test and assert `add -- <path>` and the skip. **Recommend the mock version**, since it keeps the test in-process.
- New `github_storage_writer.test.ts`: a request with `paths` is rejected.

**Block 7: Finish**
- Run lint and the related tests, then set `status: ready` in the feature file under `md2`.

There is no task-tracking tool in this session, so the blocks above are the task list.

Two decisions for you:
1. Is reporting a scheduling error via `dialogService` (without undoing the view state) OK?
2. Mocked Git or a real temp repo for the `project_files` test?

Approve to start.

5	# Data saving and commits
6	
7	Editors update application state immediately. `CommitBatcher` later coalesces repeatable edits into durable repository writes.
8	
9	## Batched save flow
10	
11	```text
12	Editor change
13	  → domain service updates in-memory state
14	  → CommitBatcher replaces that domain object's pending change
15	  → configured delay or explicit flush
16	  → renderer registers exact expected present/absent persistence outcomes
17	  → StorageService.commit creates one repository commit
18	  → optional automatic push
19	  → committed files and path changes are reconciled into application state
20	```
21	
22	`DataService.init` creates one batcher per project. Every scheduled change restarts one global trailing `react.autoCommitDelayMs` timer (30 seconds by default). This timer policy is unchanged by action identity handling.
23	
24	Pending cards use `Card.header.internalId`; pending actions use `ActionDefinition.id`; generic files use their path. Keys include change kind, preventing card, action, and file identities from colliding. Card and action paths are mutable persistence metadata.
25	
26	When flushing starts, `CommitBatcher` synchronously transfers the complete pending collection into an isolated active batch and installs a new empty pending collection. Edits received during persistence enter only the new collection. Active success discards the active batch without object-reference comparison. A successful path change rebases only newer pending source-path metadata for the same identity. Active failure restores entries only when no newer entry for that identity exists.
27	
28	A single `CommitRequest` passes both ordinary writes (`files`) and path replacements (`moves`: old path, new path, and latest content) to `StorageService.commit`.
29	
30	## Editor behavior
31	
32	### Cards and Markdown
33	
34	Card body, title, header, ordering, and policy edits update loaded files, then `CardOperations.saveFile` schedules them. All files share the batcher: editing two cards before a flush produces one request with both latest versions and a combined message.
35	
36	### Actions and filenames
37	
38	`ActionService` owns drafts by action ID, including current source path and desired target path. It also owns field and graph validation, serialization, and renderer publication. Each persistable change passes its action ID through `DataService.persistActionFile`; later committed edits replace pending content for that same ID. Non-persistable drafts stay in memory until repaired or discarded.
39	
40	An action's filename follows its label:
41	
42	1. Trim and lowercase the label.
43	2. Replace each run of non-ASCII-lowercase-letter-or-digit characters with `-`.
44	3. Remove leading and trailing `-` characters.
45	4. Add `.json` under the configured actions folder.
46	5. If another action owns the path, append `-2`, `-3`, and so on.
47
